title: Surveillance of drug-resistant bacteria in resource-limited settings: a focus on cost-effective long-read sequencing of eyedrop-associated P. aeruginosa and locally sourced metagenomic samples
text:
Surveillance of antimicrobial resistance has traditionally been centralized to research-focused institutes due to
the high cost associated with pathogen identification. Given the recent advances in long-read sequencing
technologies, we now have the potential to identify pathogens and even antimicrobial bacteriophages with low-
cost resources. It is imperative to test the capacity of long-read sequencing in the context of AMR, to reinvent
the surveillance of local infection outbreaks as a low-cost decentralized system, where resource-constraint
institutes such as California State University, Fresno can play a proactive role in monitoring and investigating
drug-resistant bacteria.

title: Miniature Ion Mobility Detector for Compact Liquid Chromatographic Analysis of Novel Psychoactive Substances
text:
There is a significant need for a small portable analyzer to detect trace amounts of new and emerging
psychoactive substances, such as fentanyl and xylazine. In this project, we will develop a miniature tandem ion
mobility spectrometer couple it to a compact capillary liquid chromatograph to fulfill this need.

title: Administrative Core (Core A)
text:
ADMINISTRATIVE CORE (CORE A) 
The Administrative Core provides the support and infrastructure for research, financial oversight, and regulatory 
monitoring. It achieves its goals by promoting clear and open communications among all SPORE investigators, 
Core leaders, Career Enhancement Program and Developmental Research Program awardees, External and 
Internal Advisory Board members, and patient advocates. Ultimately, it seeks to optimize the successful outcome 
of the translational research of this SPORE in order to improve the lives of patients with brain cancer.

title: The Consortium for Technology & Innovation in Pediatrics: CTIP 3.0
text:
Very few devices are developed, tested, and approved specifically for children due to a number of financial,
technical, and other barriers. The Consortium for Technology & Innovation in Pediatrics proposes to build on 10
years of success and continue accelerating pediatric device innovation through collaboration and support.

title: 5 D impulse mapping in the embryonic heart
text:
Congenital heart defects (CHDs) associated with the conduction of electrical impulses can be devastating
health problems. Understanding how dysfunctions arise in the early, embryonic heart is important for
discovering ways to prevent or treat these CHDs. This project will develop imaging tools to capture impulse
conduction in the living, beating heart of the early avian embryo in 3D, and map the molecular response of the
cells of the heart, under normal and abnormal conditions.

title: Metabolic Dysregulation and Cancer Risk Program: Coordinating Center
text:
The Metabolic Dysregulation and Cancer Risk Consortium (MDCRC) is being created to study the biologic
mechanisms by which obesity increases the risk of cancer in humans and will bring together several research
groups studying how obesity alters normal metabolic pathways leading to cancer risk. The Consortium
members will work together to identify common areas of data collection, and develop of a harmonized data set
to accelerate research and discovery. The MDCRC Coordinating Center will facilitate the creation of this rich
research data set, as well as provide both scientific leadership and project management for the collaborative
cross-Consortium activities.

title: Advancing our knowledge of viral membrane fusion and of IDP-membrane interactions by ESR
text:
We study how many types of viruses (SARS-CoV, flu, HIV...) attack cells, and what factors can help or hinder
this. We use a technique called Electron Spin Resonance (ESR) to learn how the parts of viruses that do the
attacks, called “fusion peptides,” are built, and how proteins in viruses interact with membranes (cell walls), to
find possible targets for new drugs to fight the viruses. We also use ESR to study how complexin, an important
protein that is related to diseases of the nervous system, interacts with membranes.

title: Non-Apoptotic Functions of Caspase-3 in Brainstem Development
text:
Precise connections between neurons in the brain are needed for understanding
sounds and localizing their sources. Defects in brain circuits that process sounds
can lead to language difficulties and problems with sound perception. This
project will explore new mechanisms that help form these brain circuits during
development.

title: Characterization of the Symptom Experience of Patients with Cutaneous Melanoma Receiving Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy
text:
The psychological symptom cluster is a common and significant problem that impacts women receiving breast
cancer treatment and is associated with several negative outcomes, including reduced functional status and
quality of life. Unfortunately, the social, environmental, and molecular mechanism(s) that drive the
development and persistence of this cluster are unknown which limits the development of effective prevention
strategies and targeted interventions. This project will examine the role of multiple social determinants of health
and epigenomic factors in the development and severity of a psychological symptom cluster in women
receiving breast cancer treatment which will provide new knowledge to guide clinical assessment and the
development of targeted interventions to mitigate the severity of this cluster.

title: Adventures in Drug Discovery: Integrating Data Science into the Science Curriculum
text: Artificial intelligence promises to accelerate the process and lower the cost of drug discovery. Integrating data science into high school chemistry and biology will prepare students with data and computing skills needed in this vital frontier of biomedical research while enhancing their learning of science and engineering expected by the Next Generation Science Standards.

title: Discovery of Novel Therapeutic Strategies for Cancer Immunotherapy
text:
Despite the unprecedented success of immune checkpoint blockade therapies that tremendously improved
patient survival in certain types of cancer, such as melanoma and non-small cell lung cancer, it has been
recognized that the response rate to current immunotherapies is still below 30% in most cancer types. In this
proposal, we aim to (1) functionally and therapeutically interrogate tumoral secreted-protein-mediated T-cell
exclusion from the tumor microenvironment to turn “cold” tumors “hot”, and (2) identify additional tumor
microenvironment-specific molecules that impair the maintenance of T-cell quantity and effector functions in
inflamed tumors to maximize the durability of anti-tumor immunity. Collectively, the proposed research will
address the urgent need in therapeutic innovations for patients with primary and acquired resistance to current
immunotherapies, and provide most patients personalized therapeutic strategies tailored to their pathological
classifications.

title: Characterization of Structural Polymorphism in Native Murine Polyomavirus from Mouse Cells
text:
Murine Polyomavirus (MPyV), a double-stranded DNA virus capable of causing tumors in newborns
and immunosuppressed mice, serves as an excellent mammalian model for the immunological and
genetic study of polyomaviruses. Overexpression of the major capsid protein VP1 in bacteria can lead
to the assembly of particles with varying diameters; however, these structures are not well
characterized and are challenging to correlate with biochemical data from cell cultures and
experimental animals. This proposal aims to dissect the structural polymorphism of native MPyV from
mouse epithelial cell lines, providing new structural insights that will enhance our understanding of
disease pathogenesis and potentially inform therapeutic strategies for polyomavirus-associated
diseases.

title: Project 2: KSHV induces tumorigenesis by harnessing differentiation in hypoxia
text:
Evidence from our recent study suggests that Kaposi’s sarcoma (KS) originates from oral mesenchymal stem
cells (MSCs) through KSHV-induced mesenchymal-to-endothelial transition (MEndT). In this proposal, we will
investigate the hypothesis that KSHV hijacks the cellular intrinsic hypoxia response to drive MSC to special
lineage differentiation and commit oncogenesis. This study will provide mechanistic insights into how KSHV
promotes MSC MEndT and oncogenic properties leading to KS.

title: Uncovering mechanisms of protection from Alzheimer's disease in CHIP using human cohorts and biosamples
text:
With advancing age, many people develop mutant clones of blood cells that circulate throughout their body.
Surprisingly, having such clones associates with protection against Alzheimer’s disease and some of these
mutant cells are able to engraft in the brain. Here, we will use genetic data and brain samples from large
cohorts and established brain banks to uncover how these mutant cells provide protection against Alzheimer’s.

title: National Succinate Dehydrogenase-deficient GIST Translational Research and Clinical Trial Consortium
text:
Succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) deficient subtype of gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) is (1) caused either
by inherited genetic or sporadic epigenetic silencing of succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) genes; (2) characterized
by variable biology that ranges from indolent growth to rapidly progressive, fatal disease; and (3) associated with
limited treatment options. This proposed U01 project will (1) combine our existing National Succinate
Dehydrogenase-deficient GIST Translational Research and Clinical Trial Consortium with unique NIH Clinical
Center resources to evaluate the efficacy of a new combinatorial treatment strategy for SDH-deficient GIST
patients; (2) create a centralized biobank of well-annotated SDH-deficient GISTs; (3) develop a network of
research laboratories with novel complementary preclinical models of SDH-deficient GIST biology; and (4)
develop new molecular tools to predict prognosis of SDH-deficient GIST. We anticipate that these aims will test
the first efficacious combination therapy for SDH-deficient GIST, create a novel resource for researchers to
improve our understanding of SDH-deficient GIST heterogeneity and biology, and molecularly define risk of
disease progression/metastasis that can be used to immediately improve SDH-deficient GIST patient care and
well-being.

title: Spatiotemporal signaling and trafficking of the mu-opioid receptor
text:
Opioids act as agonists of opioid receptors and are amongst the most effective analgesics, but they come with
serious side effects and a high potential for abuse. To date, we know little about the molecular mechanisms
mediating the beneficial and adverse actions of opioids. Our proposed studies combine proteomics and
functional genomics to discover regulators of mu-opioid receptor activation, which may identify new therapeutic
targets for pain and addiction.

title: Deep learning-enabled protein design for targeted depletion of antibiotic resistant bacterial pathogens
text:
New therapeutic approaches beyond traditional antibiotics are urgently needed to address the rapidly growing
threat of antibiotic resistance. Here, we propose to leverage our state-of-the-art deep learning methods for the
rational design of chimeric proteins, termed BacTACs, which simultaneously recognize pathogenic bacteria
and recruit host immune receptors to eliminate antibiotic-resistant strains of Acinetobacter baumannii and
Staphylococcus aureus. The design platform and resulting BacTACs will provide an orthogonal strategy to
combat a broad range of antibiotic-resistant bacteria.

title: Evaluating a cell type-specific mechanism of glutamatergic synapse function and organization
text:
Although glutamatergic excitation of interneurons is essential for maintenance of balanced signaling in the brain
and its dysregulation has been implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia, the molecular
mechanisms underlying interneuron-specific glutamatergic transmission are not well characterized. This
proposal aims to define the mechanisms by which Btbd11, a recently identified protein expressed solely in
glutamatergic synapses in interneurons, supports postsynaptic density organization and interneuron function.
The results of this proposal will provide valuable insight into a novel cell-type specific regulatory mechanism of
organization in an understudied synapse population and potentially identify a therapeutic target for increasing
inhibitory tone in psychiatric disorders.

title: Functional Connectivity, Brain Development, and Outcomes in Chiari Type I Malformation
text: Project 2: Functional Connectivity, Brain Development, and Outcomes in Chiari Type I Malformation Abstract Chiari malformation (CM) is a challenging disease. Despite its anatomically well-defined pathology characterized by herniation of the cerebellar tonsils through the foramen magnum, its clinical symptoms and indications for surgical intervention are highly variable. Here we propose advanced neuroimaging with personalized connectomics acquired longitudinally, in both surgical (pre/post posterior fossa decompression) and non-surgical CM patients, to identify imaging markers for better disease characterization and outcome prediction. We are using resting state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) to measure resting state functional connectivity (RSFC) and fractional anisotropy (FA), respectively. We are leveraging the protocols of the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study (n = 11,874), to facilitate direct comparisons to age and demographic matched control subjects from the ABCD data set, for both imaging and cognitive/emotional metrics. In addition, we are collecting Chiari Severity Index (CSI) and Chiari Health Index in Pediatrics (CHIP) data, both of which have been developed and validated by our team specifically for CM. The longitudinal arm of this project includes an adult CM cohort, which will expand the number of participants for greater power, and allow us to test developmental CM effects in the pediatric cohort. The imaging and cognitive measures will be compared at baseline before any intervention. Then within-participant comparisons will be made before and after posterior fossa decompression (PFD) surgery to identify novel imaging markers predictive of disease outcomes and response to surgery.

title: Endogenous barcoding to determine complex dynamics of adult neurogenesis in aging and Alzheimer's disease
text:
Both Alzheimer's disease and normal aging are associated with a dramatic decrease in the production of
new neurons in the hippocampus and this decrease may underlie the associated cognitive impairments.
Slowing or even reversing this decrease may be important for addressing the cognitive decline due to old age
or disease. We have recently developed a new approach for studying the birth of new neurons from stem
cells, and we will now apply this approach to determine the trajectory of neurogenesis while it is compromised
by aging and Alzheimer's disease.
